dietEvidence.body: The supposed cannibal gut contents are early crocodylomorph remains, so the direct evidence supports a diet including small crocodylomorphs, not cannibalism. The slender skull and recurved teeth indicate carnivory; prey choice beyond the preserved gut contents is inferred.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A slender early theropod known from abundant material at Ghost Ranch. The bonebed contains many individuals, but it is not direct evidence of pack hunting.
summary: A slender early theropod known from abundant material at Ghost Ranch. The bonebed contains many individuals, but it is not direct evidence of pack hunting.

discovery.body: Named by Cope, 1889. The record is known from Chinle Formation, Ghost Ranch, New Mexico. An exceptional sample of articulated skeletons from a monodominant bonebed.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: An exceptional sample of articulated skeletons from a monodominant bonebed.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: Chinle Formation, Ghost Ranch, New Mexico records the species in the Late Triassic. The numeric range used here is ≈215–201.4 Ma, combining the older Baldwin locality (radiometrically dated near 211.9 Ma) with the Rhaetian Ghost Ranch quarry; it is an occurrence estimate rather than a direct date on every specimen.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The skeleton is lightly built, with a long tail, narrow skull and recurved teeth; the forelimbs are short.

behaviour.body: The Ghost Ranch bonebed is a mass accumulation of many individuals, but it does not demonstrate pack hunting. The 2006 reanalysis removed the strongest support for cannibalism. Social behaviour and hunting coordination are unknown.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from an exceptional sample of articulated skeletons from a monodominant bonebed. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The Ghost Ranch sample is exceptional, but the famous cannibalism claim has been re-examined: the supposed juvenile gut contents are crocodylomorph remains (Nesbitt et al. 2006). The age of the quarry is latest Norian–Rhaetian; the species range used here is ≈215–201.4 Ma. Juvenile skulls show ontogenetic variation, not separate taxa.
